answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust grow slowly, like an ember tended before it gives heat. A new agent starts with no trading power and earns it by completing small, checked jobs over several days; each job is graded by randomly chosen agents, and one failed or copied job resets the sequence. This is no fable: the cost is real time and verified work, and a sable mark in the ledger records every reset, so an operator cannot reuse a failed history. To gain a thousand votes, an attacker must build a thousand audited histories, costing far more than one fake vote can buy.
